finding.claim: SQL injection in /search: query parameter q is interpolated directly into the SQL string via an f-string. An unauthenticated attacker can use UNION SELECT to read any table in shop.db, such as users or credentials, or alter the query logic.
finding.sink: db.execute(f"SELECT id, name FROM products WHERE name LIKE '%{term}%'") at app.py:12

trace.note: term taken from query string with no validation
term interpolated into the SQL via an f-string, not bound as a parameter
result rows returned to the caller as JSON, so UNION-based exfiltration is directly visible

finding.guards_checked: No authentication on the route. No input validation, escaping or length limit. No parameter binding; the sibling handlers at app.py:18 and app.py:25 do use ? placeholders, so this one is the outlier. No WAF or middleware in the app.

verdict.reason: app.py:11 reads q from request.args with no validation, app.py:12 interpolates it into the SQL via an f-string, and app.py:13 returns the rows as JSON. The route has no auth or middleware, so an anonymous caller can inject a UNION SELECT. The sibling handlers at app.py:18 and app.py:25 do use ? placeholders. I could not check which tables shop.db contains, so reading `users` or `credentials` is unconfirmed, but the injection itself is real.
